overall_structure.value: Short-range ordering (K-state) occurs in Fe-Al alloys with Al contents in the range 13-18 at.% at temperatures below 600 °C during cooling after solidification, so the as-cast Fe-14%Al lies in this short-range ordered composition range; the highest degree of short-range order was observed at 250 °C.

unmapped_findings: The yield stress of polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloys (including Fe-14%Al) at room temperature increases linearly with Al content up to 18 at.% with a hardening coefficient of about 2.2 GPa, described by Suzuki's theory of solid-solution hardening for bcc alloys; the interpolating straight lines in Fig. 3 indicate a yield-stress increase of 21 and 23 MPa per at.% Al at the 10^-2 and 10^-4 s^-1 compression rates respectively.
At -100 °C the yield stress and ultimate tensile strength of the as-cast Fe-Al alloys are higher than at room temperature by about 80 MPa.

Deformation twinning: at -100 °C twinning was observed for Al contents of 11-14% (occasionally) and above 14% (in all specimens), whereas at room temperature it was found only for the Fe-18%Al alloy; the Fe-14%Al then lies in the composition range where low-temperature twinning occurs occasionally.
Composition of the Fe-14%Al alloy (Table 1, nominal 14 at.%): real Al 13.8-14.0 at.% (7.2-7.3 wt.-%), C 20-70 wt.ppm, Si 50-60 wt.ppm, Ni <40 wt.ppm, Cu <30 wt.ppm.

Transition from ductile fracture with necking to brittle fracture without necking occurs at room temperature for 15-18 at.% Al and at -100 °C for 12-14 at.% Al, so the Fe-14%Al alloy is at the boundary of this ductile-to-brittle transition at -100 °C; at room temperature fracture strain and strain before necking show apparent relative maxima at about 8 and 12 at.% Al.

The heat treatments (e.g. 250 °C/14 d for maximum short-range order, quench from 1100 °C for minimum order) that reveal effects of atomic order were not applied to this as-cast sample; they were performed on Fe-16%Al monocrystals, and it was concluded that short-range ordering has no major impact on hardness and that only heat treatments above 600 °C significantly affect the mechanical behaviour.
